question: Describe the location of the three subatomic particles
answer: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus; electrons orbit in shells around the nucleus.

question: Compare the number of electrons in a sodium atom, sodium ion and a neon atom
answer: Sodium atom - 11 electrons; Sodium ion - 10 electrons; Neon atom - 10 electrons

question: Describe how a fluorine ion forms
answer: A fluorine atom gains 1 electron to form a fluorine ion with a -1 charge with a full outer electron shell.

question: Describe how a magnesium ion forms
answer: A magnesium atom loses 2 electrons to form a magnesium ion with a +2 charge with an empty outer election shell.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of ionic compounds
answer: High melting and boiling point; Do NOT conduct electricity when solid; Conduct electricity when molten or aqueous

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a hydrogen molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles representing hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons (one dot, one cross) in the intersection.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a chlorine molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles; place one shared pair of electrons (one dot, one cross) in the intersection, and 6 outer non-bonding electrons on each chlorine atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of an oxygen molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles; place two shared pairs of electrons (two dots, two crosses forming a double bond) in the intersection, and 4 non-bonding electrons on each oxygen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a nitrogen molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles; place three shared pairs of electrons (three dots, three crosses forming a triple bond) in the intersection, and 2 non-bonding electrons on each nitrogen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a methane molecule
answer: Draw a central carbon atom overlapping with four surrounding hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons (one dot, one cross) in each overlapping region.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a carbon dioxide molecule
answer: Draw a central carbon atom overlapping with two oxygen atoms on either side; place two shared pairs of electrons in each overlapping region (forming two double bonds).

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of an ammonia molecule
answer: Draw a central nitrogen atom overlapping with three hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons in each overlapping region, and one non-bonding lone pair on the nitrogen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of an oxygen difluoride molecule
answer: Draw a central oxygen atom overlapping with two fluorine atoms; place one shared pair of electrons in each overlapping region, two lone pairs on oxygen, and three lone pairs on each fluorine.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of small covalent molecules
answer: Low melting and boiling point; Do NOT conduct electricity; The larger the molecule the higher the melting and boiling point

question: Explain why bromine has a higher boiling point than chlorine
answer: The bromine atoms are larger meaning the molecules are larger. Therefore the intermolecular forces are stronger. Therefore more energy is required to break the forces. This makes the boiling point be higher.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of giant covalent structures
answer: Very high melting and boiling point; Hard; Brittle

question: Explain the limitations of the simple atomic model
answer: All particles are shown as spheres; Spheres are solid; No forces shown

question: Define 'delocalised electrons'
answer: Electrons that are free to move

question: Describe the structure of a metal
answer: Giant metallic lattice; Positive metal ions in layers; Delocalised electrons

question: Explain why metals are soft
answer: Positive ions are all the same size; Ions are in layers; Forces between the layers are weak; Layers can slide

question: Explain why metals can conduct electricity
answer: Delocalised electrons are free to move; Charge can flow through the lattice

question: Define an alloy
answer: A mixture of metals

question: Compare the structure of a metal and an alloy
answer: Metals have same-sized positive ions in layers.; Alloys have different-sized positive ions in distorted layers.; Both have delocalised electrons

question: Explain why alloys are harder than metals
answer: Alloys have positive ions with different sizes. This means that they are in distorted layers. The layers cannot slide as easily in an alloy.

question: List 6 properties of metals
answer: Conduct electricity; High melting and boiling point; Conduct thermal energy (heat); Malleable; Ductile; Lustrous / shiny

question: Explain why metals are malleable
answer: Positive ions are all the same size; Ions are in layers; Forces between the layers are weak; Layers can slide

question: Describe the 3 properties of diamond
answer: Very hard / rigid; Very high melting and boiling point; Does NOT conduct electricity

question: Explain why diamond is very hard / rigid
answer: There are 4 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom in a giant covalent lattice. A lot of energy is required to break the covalent bonds.

question: Explain why diamond has a very high melting point
answer: There are 4 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom in a giant covalent lattice. A lot of energy is required to break the covalent bonds.

question: Explain why diamond does NOT conduct electricity
answer: There are no delocalised electrons so no charge can flow through the lattice

question: Describe the structure of diamond
answer: 4 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom; Giant covalent lattice

question: Describe 3 properties of graphite
answer: Soft / slippery; Very high melting and boiling point; Does conduct electricity

question: Explain why graphite is slippery
answer: The forces between the layers are weak which require little energy to break. Therefore the layers can slide.

question: Explain why graphite is used as a lubricant
answer: The forces between the layers are weak which require little energy to break. Therefore the layers can slide.

question: Explain why graphite has a very high melting and boiling point
answer: 3 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom.; Giant covalent lattice.; A lot of energy is required to break the covalent bonds

question: Explain why graphite as electrodes in the process of electrolysis
answer: The delocalised electrons can move and allow charge to flow through the layers.

question: Explain why graphite conducts electricity
answer: The delocalised electrons can move and allow charge to flow through the layers.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a water molecule (H2O).
answer: Draw a central oxygen atom overlapping with two hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons in each overlapping region, and two non-bonding lone pairs on the oxygen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a hydrogen chloride molecule (HCl).
answer: Draw an overlapping carbon/hydrogen or hydrogen/chlorine region; place one shared pair of electrons in the intersection, and 6 non-bonding outer electrons on the chlorine atom.

question: Describe how an oxide ion (O2-) forms from an oxygen atom.
answer: An oxygen atom gains 2 electrons to form an oxide ion with a -2 charge.

question: Describe how a calcium ion (Ca2+) forms from a calcium atom.
answer: A calcium atom loses 2 electrons to form a calcium ion with a +2 charge.

question: Describe how sodium and chlorine react to form sodium chloride in terms of electron transfer.
answer: Sodium loses 1 outer electron to form a Na+ ion; chlorine gains that 1 electron to form a Cl- ion; oppositely charged ions attract via strong electrostatic forces.

question: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons (OIL RIG).
answer: Oxidation is the loss of electrons; Reduction is the gain of electrons.

question: Write the half-equation for the formation of a magnesium ion from a magnesium atom during oxidation.
answer: Mg ➔ Mg2+ + 2e-

question: Write the half-equation for the formation of a fluoride ion from a fluorine molecule during reduction.
Explain why magnesium undergoes oxidation when reacting with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.
answer: Magnesium loses 2 electrons from its outer shell to form a Mg2+ ion (oxidation is the loss of electrons).

question: Explain why oxygen undergoes reduction when reacting with sodium to form sodium oxide.
answer: Oxygen gains 2 electrons into its outer shell to form an O2- ion (reduction is the gain of electrons).

question: Explain why small covalent molecules (such as water or methane) generally have low melting points.
answer: They have weak intermolecular forces between molecules that require very little energy to break, even though the covalent bonds within molecules are strong.

question: Explain the trend in boiling points as the molecular size of alkanes/covalent molecules increases.
answer: As molecular size increases, the strength of the intermolecular forces increases, so more energy is required to overcome them, resulting in higher boiling points.

question: Explain why magnesium oxide (MgO) has a significantly higher melting point than sodium chloride (NaCl).
answer: MgO contains doubly charged ions (Mg2+ and O2-) whereas NaCl contains singly charged ions (Na+ and Cl-); the stronger electrostatic forces between higher-charged ions require much more energy to break.

question: Compare the electrical conductivity of solid sodium chloride versus molten sodium chloride.
answer: Solid NaCl cannot conduct electricity because its ions are fixed in a rigid lattice and cannot move; molten NaCl conducts electricity because the ionic lattice breaks down, leaving ions free to move and carry charge.

question: Compare the electrical conductivity of an ionic compound in aqueous solution with a simple covalent compound like sucrose in water.
answer: An aqueous ionic compound conducts electricity because its dissolved ions are free to move and carry charge; sucrose does not conduct electricity because simple covalent molecules are uncharged.

question: Explain why polymers have higher melting points than small covalent molecules like methane.
answer: Polymer molecules are much larger, so the total intermolecular forces between the long chains are much stronger and require more energy to overcome.

question: Explain why covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity in any state.
answer: Simple covalent molecules do not contain free-moving ions or delocalised electrons, so there are no charged particles available to carry electrical current.

question: Compare what happens to the structure of sodium chloride when it melts and ice when it melts.
answer: Melting NaCl breaks strong ionic bonds between Na+ and Cl- ions; melting ice only breaks weak intermolecular forces between water molecules (covalent bonds remain intact).

question: Explain why halogens further down Group 7 (e.g., iodine vs. fluorine) are solids rather than gases at room temperature.
answer: Molecules become larger down Group 7, increasing the strength of intermolecular forces, so more energy is needed to separate iodine molecules than fluorine molecules.

question: Who created the plum pudding model?
answer: J.J. Thomson.

question: Which subatomic particle was discovered first?
answer: The electron (discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897).

question: Who created the nuclear model?
answer: Ernest Rutherford (following the alpha particle scattering experiment).

question: Who discovered neutrons?
answer: James Chadwick (in 1932).

question: Who created the model where electrons are in shells?
answer: Niels Bohr (he suggested electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances/energy levels).

question: Explain the results of Rutherford's gold foil experiment.
answer: Most alpha particles passed straight through (atom is mostly empty space); some were deflected at small angles (nucleus is positively charged); a tiny fraction bounced straight back (mass is concentrated in a tiny central nucleus).

question: Explain why the reactivity of group 7 elements decreases as you go down the group.
answer: Group 7 elements react by gaining 1 electron into their outer shell. As you go down the group, atomic radius and inner shell shielding increase. The positive nucleus has a weaker electrostatic attraction for an incoming outer electron, making it harder to gain an electron.

question: Describe what you would see if sodium reacted with chlorine.
answer: The green chlorine gas reacts with silver/grey sodium metal. A vigorous reaction occurs with a bright yellow/orange flame. White smoke/fumes are produced, which settle as a white solid (sodium chloride).

question: Define an element.
answer: A substance made of only one type of atom with each atom containing the same number of protons.

question: Define a compound.
answer: A substance consisting of two or more different elements chemically bonded together in fixed proportions.

question: Define a mixture.
answer: Two or more elements or compounds that are mixed together but not chemically combined. They can be separated by physical methods.

question: Describe how to arrange electrons in shells.
answer: Fill shells from inside out: 1st shell holds up to 2 electrons, 2nd shell holds up to 8, 3rd shell holds up to 8.

question: Compare the relative charge, mass and location of the 3 subatomic particles found in a fluorine atom.
answer: Protons: relative mass 1, charge +1, located in nucleus. Neutrons: relative mass 1, charge 0, located in nucleus. Electrons: relative mass ~1/2000 (very small), charge -1, located orbiting in electron shells.

question: Compare the mass number and atomic number of an atom.
answer: Atomic number: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom (defines the element). Mass number: The total number of protons plus neutrons in the nucleus.

question: Define solvent.
answer: The liquid in which a solute dissolves to form a solution (e.g., water).

question: Define solute.
answer: The solid or substance that dissolves in a solvent (e.g., salt).

question: Define solution.
answer: A mixture formed when a solute dissolves completely in a solvent.

question: Describe the 5 main separation methods of mixtures.
answer: Filtration: insoluble solid from liquid. Crystallisation: soluble solid from liquid. Simple Distillation: solvent from solution. Fractional Distillation: mixture of liquids with different boiling points. Paper Chromatography: soluble substances like dyes.

question: Define an isotope.
answer: An atom of an element with the same number of protons and electrons and a different number of neutrons.

question: Describe 3 observations of Rutherford's gold foil experiment.
answer: Most alpha particles passed straight through undeflected. Some alpha particles were deflected at small angles. A very small number of alpha particles bounced straight back (deflected by more than 90°).

question: Explain how the 3 observations of Rutherford's gold foil experiment helped to change the model of the atom.
answer: Passed straight through: Proved atom is mostly empty space. Deflected at small angles: Proved nucleus has a concentrated positive charge. Bounced straight back: Proved mass of atom is concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.

question: Describe what John Dalton suggested about the atom.
answer: Dalton suggested that atoms were tiny, indivisible spheres that could not be divided or split into smaller parts.

question: Describe the model of the atom by JJ Thomson.
answer: The plum pudding model: a sphere of positive charge with negatively charged electrons embedded within it.

question: Describe the atomic model suggested by Ernest Rutherford.
answer: The nuclear model: a tiny, positively charged nucleus at the centre containing most of the atom's mass, surrounded by negatively charged electrons, with mostly empty space between them.

question: Explain how Niels Bohr changed our understanding of the model of the atom.
answer: Bohr calculated and proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels (shells) at specific distances from the nucleus, preventing the atom from collapsing.

question: Describe what James Chadwick discovered.
answer: Chadwick discovered the neutron — an uncharged (neutral) particle with the same mass as a proton, located in the nucleus.

question: Describe Mendeleev's periodic table.
answer: Mendeleev arranged elements primarily in order of increasing atomic weight, aligned elements with similar chemical properties into columns, and left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties.

question: Compare the modern periodic table to that of Mendeleev.
answer: Modern: arranged by atomic number (protons), includes noble gases, no gaps needed. Mendeleev: arranged primarily by atomic weight, left gaps for undiscovered elements, lacked Group 0 elements.

question: Explain why Dmitri Mendeleev's periodic table came to be accepted.
answer: Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties. When these elements (e.g., gallium, germanium) were later discovered, their properties matched his predictions closely, proving his table was correct.

question: Explain why the reactivity of alkali metals increases as you go down group 1.
answer: Group 1 elements react by losing 1 electron. As you go down the group, atomic radius and shielding increase. The outer electron is further from the nucleus with less electrostatic attraction, making it lost more easily.

question: Explain how the reactivity of alkali metals changes as you go up the group.
answer: Group 1 elements react by losing 1 electron. As you go up the group, atoms get smaller with less shielding. The outer electron is closer to the nucleus with stronger attraction, so it is lost less easily, making elements less reactive.

question: Explain why the reactivity of halogens increases as you go up group 7.
answer: As you go up Group 7, atoms have fewer electron shells (smaller radius) and less shielding. The positive nucleus has a stronger electrostatic attraction for an incoming electron, so an electron is gained more easily.

question: Explain why the reactivity of halogens decreases as you go down the group.
answer: Group 7 elements react by gaining 1 electron. As you go down the group, atomic radius and shielding increase. The outer shell is further from the nucleus, weakening attraction for an incoming electron and making it harder to gain.

question: Name 4 properties of metals.
answer: Good conductors of electricity and heat, high melting and boiling points, malleable and ductile, shiny/lustrous when freshly cut.

question: Name 4 properties of non-metals.
answer: Poor conductors of electricity and heat (insulators), low melting and boiling points, dull in appearance, brittle when solid.

question: Compare the properties of metals and non-metals.
answer: Metals: high melting points, good conductors, malleable, form positive ions. Non-metals: low melting points, electrical insulators, brittle, form negative ions or share electrons.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of halogens.
answer: Exist as diatomic molecules (e.g., Cl2), form ionic salts with metals, melting/boiling points and densities increase down the group.

question: Describe the 2 main properties of alkali metals.
answer: Soft (can be cut with a knife) with low density (first three float on water), low melting points, highly reactive with air and water.

question: Name the following groups: 1, 7 and 0.
answer: Group 1: Alkali Metals; Group 7: Halogens; Group 0: Noble Gases.

question: Define atomic number.
answer: The number of protons in an atom.

question: Define mass number.
answer: The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.

question: Describe the method of filtration.
answer: Fold a piece of filter paper into a cone and place it into a filter funnel over a conical flask. Pour the mixture of insoluble solid and liquid into the funnel. Liquid (filtrate) passes through while insoluble solid (residue) stays on paper.

question: Describe the method of crystallisation.
answer: Pour solution into an evaporating basin and heat gently to evaporate solvent until reaching point of crystallisation. Remove from heat to cool slowly so crystals form. Filter out crystals and dry them in a warm oven or with filter paper.

question: Describe the method of distillation.
answer: Heat the liquid mixture in a flask so the component with lowest boiling point evaporates. The vapor rises and enters a condenser cooled by running water, where it condenses back into a liquid to be collected.

question: Describe five observations you would see if you placed Sodium into water
answer: It floats, disappears, melts into a sphere, moves on the surface of the water, has a yellow flame

question: Name groups 1, 7 and 0 of the periodic table
answer: Group 1 - alkali metals, Group 7 - halogens, Group 0 - noble gases

question: Describe where you find metals and non-metals on the periodic table
answer: Metals - left side of the table; Non-metals - right side of the table

question: Describe the electron configuration for an atom of fluorine
answer: Fluorine has an atomic number of 9 (9 electrons): 2, 7 (2 electrons in the inner shell, 7 in the outer shell).

question: Explain why the reactivity of group 1 metals increases as you go down the group
answer:
Group 1 metals react by losing 1 outer electron.

As you go down the group, the atoms get larger because they have more electron shells.

The outer electron is further from the nucleus, leading to increased shielding from inner shells.

This results in a weaker electrostatic attraction between the positive nucleus and the outer electron, so the outer electron is lost more easily.

question: Explain why neon is not very reactive
answer: The outer shell of electrons is full.

question: Explain the reactivity of group 0 elements
answer: Group 0 elements are unreactive (inert) because all their atoms have a stable, full outer shell of electrons (a stable octet, or duet for Helium), so they do not easily form chemical bonds.

question: Compare a group and a period in the periodic table
answer: A group is a column. A period is a row.

question: Describe, using a word equation, the reaction between iron oxide and sulfuric acid
answer: iron oxide + sulfuric acid -> iron sulfate + water

question: Describe, using a word equation, the reaction between sodium carbonate and hydrochloric acid
answer: sodium carbonate + hydrochloric acid -> sodium chloride + carbon dioxide + water

question: Explain what will happen if magnesium and iron chloride are reacted together
answer: A displacement reaction will occur because magnesium is more reactive than iron. Magnesium will displace iron to form magnesium chloride solution and solid iron.

question: Describe the test for oxygen
answer: Insert a glowing splint into a test tube of gas; if oxygen is present, the splint will relight.

question: Describe the test for hydrogen
answer: Hold a lit splint near the open mouth of a test tube of gas; if hydrogen is present, it burns with a squeaky pop.

question: Describe the test for carbon dioxide
answer: Bubble the gas through limewater (calcium hydroxide solution); if carbon dioxide is present, the limewater turns cloudy/milky.

question: Describe the test for chlorine
answer: Hold damp blue litmus paper at the mouth of a test tube containing the gas; if chlorine is present, the litmus paper turns red and then bleaches white.

question: Name the reactivity series
answer: Potassium, Sodium, Lithium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Carbon, Zinc, Iron, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold

question: Write the word equation for when Magnesium and Oxygen react together
answer: magnesium + oxygen -> magnesium oxide

question: Explain what will happen when zinc oxide and carbon react
answer: Carbon will reduce zinc oxide in a displacement reaction because carbon is more reactive than zinc. Carbon removes oxygen from zinc oxide to form zinc metal and carbon dioxide (or carbon monoxide).

question: Explain what will happen when potassium and oxygen react
answer: Potassium will react vigorously with oxygen in an oxidation reaction to form a white ionic compound, potassium oxide

question: Explain what will happen when copper sulfate reacts with magnesium
answer: A displacement reaction will occur because magnesium is more reactive than copper. The blue copper sulfate solution will fade/turn colourless as magnesium sulfate forms, and a brown/pink solid (copper) will deposit.

question: Write a method for investigating how the reactivity of 4 different metals is different
answer:
Measure equal volumes of dilute hydrochloric acid into 4 separate insulated cups/test tubes using a measuring cylinder.
Record the starting temperature of the acid in each tube using a thermometer.
Add a fixed, equal mass and surface area (e.g., granules/powder) of each of the 4 metals (e.g., magnesium, zinc, iron, copper) to separate tubes.
Record the highest temperature reached during each reaction.
Rank the reactivity based on temperature rise: the metal causing the largest temperature increase is the most reactive (copper will show no change).

question: Define a displacement reaction
answer: A chemical reaction in which a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive element in its compound.

question: Describe the word equation for the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon
answer: zinc oxide + carbon -> zinc + carbon dioxide

question: Define an ore
answer: A rock or mineral that contains enough of a metal or metal compound to make it economically worthwhile to extract the metal.

question: Name the 4 state symbols
answer:
(s): Solid

(l): Liquid

(g): Gas

(aq): Aqueous (dissolved in water)

question: Describe the method of filtration
answer: Place filter paper in a funnel. Pour the solution through and allow the solid to remain in the filter paper and the the solution to pass through the filter.
